1	import type {
2	  AgentJournalApprovalMatchedAskRule,
3	  AgentJournalApprovalSubject
4	} from '../../../src/shared/agent-session-journal-types'
5	import { clipWithEllipsis } from '../text/whole-character-cut'
6	import { isClaudePlanFeedbackOptionLabel } from './claude-plan-permission'
7	import { parseAgentQuestion } from './mobile-native-chat-question'
8	import { codeFenceStarts, collectOptionLists } from './mobile-native-chat-question-lists'
9	
10	// Agent permission asks (e.g. Claude/Codex "Do you want to proceed?") surface
11	// as plain TUI text in the agent's last assistant message — there is no
12	// structured permission event on mobile. We detect them heuristically so the
13	// native chat can render tappable Allow/Deny buttons instead of forcing the
14	// user to type into the composer. Be conservative: only fire when the agent is
15	// actually paused (blocked/waiting) AND the text reads like an approval ask.
16	
17	/** A detected permission prompt, rendered as a card with tappable options.
18	 *  Each option's `send` is the literal string to write back to the agent
19	 *  (e.g. "y", "1") when the user taps it. */
20	export type MobileChatPermission = {
21	  title: string
22	  displayName?: string
23	  description?: string
24	  decisionReason?: string
25	  blockedPath?: string
26	  matchedAskRule?: AgentJournalApprovalMatchedAskRule
27	  subject?: AgentJournalApprovalSubject
28	  detail?: string
29	  command?: string
30	  /** Structured prompt identity, present only when the host can cancel it exactly. */
31	  prompt?: { itemId: string; expectedRevision: number }
32	  options: Array<{ label: string; send: string }>
33	}
34	
35	/** Identity of the prompt, not of its rendering. The card keys its remount on
36	 *  this, and its in-flight guard is component-local, so keying on the whole
37	 *  object remounted the card whenever the screen parse flipped its options —
38	 *  re-enabling the buttons mid-send, with no "waiting for agent" left, while
39	 *  the first keystroke was still crossing the relay. Options are presentation;
40	 *  what identifies the prompt is what it is asking. */
41	export function mobileChatPermissionKey(permission: MobileChatPermission): string {
42	  return [permission.title, permission.command ?? '', permission.detail ?? ''].join('\u0000')
43	}
44	
45	const ESCAPE = String.fromCharCode(27)
46	
47	/** Parse the live `agentStatus.interactivePrompt` approval envelope
48	 *  (`{ approval: { tool, summary } }`, emitted by the host on a PermissionRequest)
49	 *  into an Allow/Deny card. This is the reliable, agent-emitted signal — unlike
50	 *  detectAgentPermission it doesn't depend on heuristic text parsing. The default
51	 *  sends (number for allow, Escape for deny) match the common TUI approval prompt;
52	 *  detectAgentPermission still takes precedence when it can read the real numbered
53	 *  options from the prompt text. */
54	export function parseApprovalFromStatus(
55	  interactivePrompt: string | undefined | null
56	): MobileChatPermission | null {
57	  if (!interactivePrompt) {
58	    return null
59	  }
60	  let parsed: unknown
61	  try {
62	    parsed = JSON.parse(interactivePrompt)
63	  } catch {
64	    return null
65	  }
66	  if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object') {
67	    return null
68	  }
69	  const approval = (parsed as { approval?: unknown }).approval
70	  if (!approval || typeof approval !== 'object') {
71	    return null
72	  }
73	  const tool = (approval as { tool?: unknown }).tool
74	  if (typeof tool !== 'string' || tool.length === 0) {
75	    return null
76	  }
77	  const summary = (approval as { summary?: unknown }).summary
78	  return {
79	    title: `Allow ${tool}?`,
80	    detail: typeof summary === 'string' && summary.length > 0 ? summary : undefined,
81	    options: [
82	      { label: 'Allow', send: '1' },
83	      { label: 'Deny', send: ESCAPE }
84	    ]
85	  }
86	}
87	
88	type PermissionInput = {
89	  state?: string
90	  lastAssistantMessage?: string
91	  toolName?: string
92	  toolInput?: unknown
93	}
94	
95	// States where the agent is paused waiting on the human. Only these can yield a
96	// permission prompt — a "working" agent is mid-turn and must not be answered.
97	const PAUSED_STATES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(['blocked', 'waiting'])
98	
99	// Phrases that read as an approval request. Kept broad but anchored to
100	// approval/permission language so ordinary prose doesn't trip detection.
101	const PERMISSION_PATTERNS: RegExp[] = [
102	  /\bpermission\b/i,
103	  /\bapprove\b/i,
104	  /\bapproval\b/i,
105	  /\ballow\b/i,
106	  /\bdeny\b/i,
107	  /\bgrant\b/i,
108	  /\bauthorize\b/i,
109	  /\bdo you want to\b/i,
110	  /\bwould you like to\b/i,
111	  /\bproceed\?/i,
112	  /\bconfirm\b/i,
113	  /\(y\/n\)/i,
114	  /\by\/n\b/i,
115	  /\byes\/no\b/i,
116	  /\bplease confirm\b/i
117	]
118	
119	function looksLikePermissionAsk(text: string): boolean {
120	  return PERMISSION_PATTERNS.some((re) => re.test(text))
121	}
122	
123	// How an option of an approval menu begins, once the emphasis in front of it
124	// is gone: a way to say yes, or a way to say no. Claude Code's plan review
125	// says no with "Tell Claude what to change" (claude-plan-permission.ts).
126	// "Decline", "Not now" and "Not yet" are agent prose, no captured screen: a
127	// menu of "Approve / Decline" or "Yes / Not now" lost its card to the question
128	// card without them (2026-10-01). "Not sure" is no way to say no.
129	const AFFIRMS = /^(?:yes|allow|approve|always|proceed)(?![\p{L}\p{N}])/iu
130	const REFUSES =
131	  /^(?:no|deny|decline|reject|cancel|skip|not\s+(?:now|yet)|don['’]t|do\s+not)(?![\p{L}\p{N}])/iu
132	
133	function approvalAnswer(label: string): 'yes' | 'no' | null {
134	  const plain = label.replace(/^[*_`]+/, '')
135	  if (AFFIRMS.test(plain)) {
136	    return 'yes'
137	  }
138	  return REFUSES.test(plain) || isClaudePlanFeedbackOptionLabel(plain) ? 'no' : null
139	}
140	
141	/** Every label answers the ask: "Yes", "No, and tell Claude…", "Allow". */
142	function readsAsApproval(labels: readonly string[]): boolean {
143	  return labels.every((label) => approvalAnswer(label) !== null)
144	}
145	
146	/**
147	 * The reply's approval menu: a numbered list, outside code fences, of two or
148	 * more options that all answer the ask, with a way to say yes AND a way to
149	 * say no. Steps that all begin "Skip…", "Cancel…" are still steps. With more
150	 * than one, the last: the menu is what the reply ends on, and a list of
151	 * findings or notes around it is not choices. Null when there is none: a
152	 * numbered list that is not a menu sent a step, or a choice of database, as
153	 * the answer to "Do you want to go ahead?" (2026-09-30).
154	 */
155	function approvalMenu(text: string): MobileChatPermission['options'] | null {
156	  const lines = text.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n').split('\n')
157	  const lists = collectOptionLists(lines, codeFenceStarts(lines))
158	  for (let at = lists.length - 1; at >= 0; at--) {
159	    const { items } = lists[at]
160	    const options = items.flatMap(({ label, token }) =>
161	      token != null && /^\d+$/.test(token) ? [{ label, send: token }] : []
162	    )
163	    const answers = options.map(({ label }) => approvalAnswer(label))
164	    if (
165	      options.length >= 2 &&
166	      options.length === items.length &&
167	      answers.includes('yes') &&
168	      answers.includes('no') &&
169	      !answers.includes(null)
170	    ) {
171	      return options
172	    }
173	  }
174	  return null
175	}
176	
177	// Whether a label reads as "allow for every future call" rather than just once.
178	function isAlwaysLabel(text: string): boolean {
179	  return /\balways\b|don't ask again|do not ask again|for the rest|this session/i.test(text)
180	}
181	
182	// Cut at `max` code units, never through an emoji (a half drew a broken glyph).
183	function shortLabel(text: string, max = 40): string {
184	  return clipWithEllipsis(text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim(), max)
185	}
186	
187	function firstLine(text: string): string {
188	  return text.split('\n')[0]?.trim() ?? ''
189	}
190	
191	/**
192	 * Heuristically detect an agent permission ask from its paused-state context.
193	 * Returns a renderable prompt, or null when the agent is working, the text
194	 * doesn't read like an approval request, or it asks the reader to choose
195	 * (the question card's, which a permission card would hide).
196	 */
197	export function detectAgentPermission(input: PermissionInput): MobileChatPermission | null {
198	  // Only answer a genuinely paused agent. A working agent is mid-turn.
199	  if (!input.state || !PAUSED_STATES.has(input.state)) {
200	    return null
201	  }
202	
203	  const text = typeof input.lastAssistantMessage === 'string' ? input.lastAssistantMessage : ''
204	  if (!text.trim()) {
205	    return null
206	  }
207	
208	  if (!looksLikePermissionAsk(text)) {
209	    return null
210	  }
211	
212	  const detail = shortLabel(firstLine(text), 160) || undefined
213	
214	  // Prefer an explicit numbered menu ("1. Yes  2. No, and tell…") — its labels
215	  // and send-digits come straight from the agent, so no guessing.
216	  const menu = approvalMenu(text)
217	  if (menu) {
218	    return { title: 'Permission requested', detail, options: menu }
219	  }
220	  // "Which database do you want to use? 1. Postgres 2. SQLite" asks for a
221	  // choice, not a yes: leave it to the question card. A list of Yes and No
222	  // bullets, or one lone "1. Yes", still asks for a yes, and so do steps
223	  // around a "(y/n)" ask, which draw no question card at all.
224	  const question = parseAgentQuestion(text)
225	  if (question && !readsAsApproval(question.options)) {
226	    return null
227	  }
228	
229	  // Otherwise fall back to a y/n prompt. We surface "Allow always" only when the
230	  // text actually offers a persistent option, to avoid sending a token the agent
231	  // doesn't understand.
232	  const options: MobileChatPermission['options'] = [
233	    { label: 'Allow', send: 'y' },
234	    { label: 'Deny', send: 'n' }
235	  ]
236	  if (isAlwaysLabel(text)) {
237	    options.splice(1, 0, { label: 'Allow always', send: 'a' })
238	  }
239	
240	  return { title: 'Permission requested', detail, options }
241	}

716	  kept apart from `live=` (`stopRunningTaskIds`, `stopRunningTaskIdsAt` on the
717	  beacon, replaced on every Stop). Before this, a `live=` repaint about 5 s after
718	  the launching turn ended retired the workflow as "Completed" and flickered it
719	  back at every later Stop (reviewed with the real Stop and status-line scripts,
720	  2026-09-30). It still ends on its own notification, a `done=`, a pane `done`,
721	  or a later Stop whose `run=` lacks it; a launch after the last Stop spoke is
722	  not judged by it. No Stop yet: nothing retires it.
723	- **Attribution rule.** A lane names no workflow, so lanes are counted on a card
724	  only when nothing says they could be another workflow's: exactly one workflow
725	  running in the loaded window; a Stop has spoken (`stopRunningTaskIds`) and
726	  every id on its `run=` is a launch the window showed (a workflow launched
727	  above the window is running and would be on that list, unlaunched here); the
728	  window reaches back to before that Stop (so a launch since then is in it, not
729	  above it); the lane started after this workflow's launch; the host does not
730	  say the pane is done. `live=` plays no part: it is rebuilt every repaint and
731	  cannot vouch for what ran before it. Otherwise the lanes are left as they
732	  were, ordinary agent rows, not attributed and not folded. Counted lanes are
733	  taken off the running list and not counted twice in "N running tasks". A lane
734	  a finished workflow left on a stale roster started before the next launch, so
735	  it is not counted on it.
736	- **Finished**: the notification moves it to Finished. The `<usage>` block is
737	  read from after `</result>` (the result is model-written and can quote one),
738	  and gives "N agents", "N tokens", "N failed" (`agents_error`, danger tone) and
739	  "N skipped" when non-zero. The phase titles stay on the card.
